'''Fulvio Cacace''' (died 1 December 2003<ref name=obit2003/>) was an Italian [[chemist]].

In 1963, while at the [[Sapienza University of Rome]], he devised the [[decay technique]] for the study of [[organic chemistry|organic]] [[radical (chemistry)|radicals]] and [[carbenium]] cations.<ref name=fcac1963/><ref name=fcac1970/>  The technique is based on the preparation of compounds containing the [[radioactivity|radioactive]] [[isotope]] [[tritium]] in place of common [[hydrogen]].  When the tritium undergoes [[beta decay]], it is turned into a [[helium-3]] atom, that detaches from the parent molecule, leaving the desired cation or radical behind.

The technique has made it possible to study the chemistry of a vast number of such radicals and ions, in all sorts of environments, including solids, liquids, and gases.  In particular, it has provided much of the knowledge of the chemistry of the [[helium hydride ion]], specifically {{chem2|[^{3}He^{3}H](+)}}.<ref name=sper1993/><ref name=akul1976/><ref name=fcac1970/>

==Some publications==
* (1966) "A Tracer Study of the Reactions of Ionic Intermediates Formed by Nuclear Decay of Tritiated Molecules. I. Methane-t4".<ref name=fcac1966/>
* (1970) "Gaseous Carbonium Ions from the Decay of Tritiated Molecules".<ref name=fcac1970/>
* (1973) "Gas-phase reaction of tert-butyl ions with arenes. Remarkable selectivity of a gaseous, charged [[electrophile]]".<ref name=fcac1973/>
* (1976) "Gas-phase alkylation of xylenes by tert-butyl(1+) ions".<ref name=giac1976/>
* (1977) "Aromatic substitution in the gas phase. Ambident behavior of phenol toward t-C4H9+ cations".<ref name=atti1977/>
* (1977) "Aromatic substitution in the liquid phase by bona fide free methyl cations. Alkylation of benzene and toluene".<ref name=fcac1977a/>
* (1978) "Aromatic substitutions by [{{chem2|^{3}H3}}]methyl decay ions. A comparative study of the gas- and liquid-phase attack on benzene and toluene".<ref name=fcac1978/>
* (1979) "Gas-phase reaction of free isopropyl ions with phenol and [[anisole]]".<ref name=atti1979/>
* (1980) "Aromatic substitution in the gas phase. A comparative study of the alkylation of benzene and toluene with C3H7+ ions from the protonation of [[cyclopropane]] and propene".<ref name=atti1980/>
* (1981) "Aromatic substitution in the gas phase. Alkylation of arenes by gaseous C4H9+ cations".<ref name=fcac1981/>
* (1982) "On the formation of adduct ions in gas-phase aromatic substitution".<ref name=fcac1982/>
* (1982) "Alkylation of nitriles with gaseous carbenium ions. The Ritter reaction in the dilute gas state".<ref name=fcac1982b/>
* (1982) "Aromatic substitution in the gas phase. Alkylation of arenes by C4H9+ ions from the protonation of C4 alkenes and cycloalkanes with gaseous Brønsted acids".<ref name=fcac1982c/>
* (1983) "Aromatic substitution in the gas phase. Intramolecular selectivity of the reaction of aniline with charged electrophiles".<ref name=atti1983/>
* (1984) "Gas-phase reactions of free phenylium cations with C3H6 hydrocarbons".<ref name=colo1984/>
* (1985) "Intramolecular selectivity of the alkylation of substituted anilines by gaseous cations".<ref name=atti1985/>
* (1986) "Temperature dependence of the substrate and positional selectivity of the aromatic substitution by gaseous tert-butyl cation".<ref name=fcac1986/>
* (1990) "Nuclear Decay Techniques in Ion Chemistry".<ref name=fcac1990/>
* (1992) "Proton shifts in gaseous arenium ions and their role in the gas-phase aromatic substitution by free Me3C+ and Me3Si+ [tert-butyl and trimethylsilyl] cations".<ref name=fcac1992/>
* (1993) "Interannular proton transfer in thermal arenium ions from the gas-phase alkylation of 1,2-diphenylethane".<ref name=fcac1993/>
